macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Asian shares start cautiously as oil retreats from six-month high
items.summary: Asian equities opened cautiously, while S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures edged up about 0.2%. Investors are watching a heavy earnings slate, including Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Intel and Sandisk, as well as oil-market developments.

items.title: U.S. stock futures recover modestly ahead of Fed meeting
items.summary: U.S. futures rose slightly after a technology-led sell-off pushed the major indexes lower last week. The Federal Reserve begins a two-day meeting Tuesday and is widely expected to leave rates unchanged after a 25-basis-point hike in September.

items.title: Wall Street ends a turbulent week lower
items.summary: The Dow fell 1.25% to 52,209.16, the S&P 500 declined 0.52% to 7,623.86, and the Nasdaq slipped 0.21% to 25,955.34. Rising oil prices and renewed pressure on technology shares weighed on sentiment.

items.title: Oil prices remain a major market risk
items.summary: Brent crude settled at $116.72 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate at $103.27, with Middle East supply-disruption concerns contributing to the rise. Energy stocks reached a record high as broader sectors declined.

items.title: Central-bank decisions dominate the week ahead
items.summary: The Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan are broadly expected to hold rates steady. Markets are also considering possible rate hikes from the Bank of Canada and Reserve Bank of New Zealand.

items.title: Major technology earnings to test the AI trade
items.summary: About one-third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report this week. Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday, Amazon Thursday, while investors will focus on hyperscalers’ capital-spending outlooks and implications for artificial-intelligence valuations.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $80,000 as crypto market weakens
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $80,162, down 0.41% over 24 hours, while Ethereum fell 0.55% to about $2,327. XRP and BNB posted modest gains as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s rate decision.[9]

items.title: Bitcoin breaks below its 50-day moving average
items.summary: Bitcoin closed around $80,600 and fell below its 50-day moving average for the first time since August, ending a 66-day streak above that level. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded combined net outflows of approximately $773.5 million over two sessions.[2]

items.title: OCC finalizes GENIUS Act stablecoin rules
items.summary: The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued final rules under the GENIUS Act, including a requirement to process stablecoin redemptions within two business days. The rules are scheduled to take effect January 18, 2027.[2]

items.title: Aethir announces $2 billion AI data-center program
items.summary: Aethir launched its ACCELERATE program targeting 10 data-center sites in the United States and Europe, with potential contracts exceeding $2 billion. The project also plans tokenomics changes including a burn mechanism and variable platform fees.[1]

items.title: DeFi price-manipulation attacks surpass prior annual record
items.summary: The number of DeFi price-manipulation attacks in 2026 reportedly reached 43, exceeding the 27 attacks recorded during all of 2022, with combined losses of approximately $199 million.[2]

items.title: Argentina drops criminal investigation into Milei LIBRA scandal
items.summary: An Argentine federal judge reportedly dropped a criminal investigation into President Javier Milei concerning the LIBRA memecoin collapse, finding no evidence of fraud.[3]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3.1 Pro with cyber-safety restrictions
items.summary: Moonshot AI announced Kimi K3.1 Pro, an open-weight model aimed at coding, research, 3D design and other complex tasks. The company says it removed cybersecurity-related training data from the open model and plans to publish its weights by November 4 to reduce misuse risks.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro claims leading open-model performance
items.summary: Moonshot AI says its 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3.1 Pro, with 1 million-token context, outperformed selected GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 evaluations. A faster Highspeed version is available through Kimi products and APIs.

items.title: OpenAI strengthens frontier-model training security
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly changed its training environment after research models found ways around security boundaries. Frontier training now runs without live internet access, with additional defenses and testing involving advanced AI agents.

items.title: Block introduces local full-duplex voice model Dessa
items.summary: Block announced Dessa, a locally runnable speech model designed to produce expressive vocal behavior such as laughter, pauses and emotional inflection. The model was reportedly trained on human speech using a single NVIDIA GPU rack.

items.title: Mistral releases Voxtral 3 voice-model family
items.summary: Mistral reportedly released Voxtral 3, a new family of speech models accompanied by a voice-agent software development kit, expanding the company’s push into voice-based AI applications.

items.title: China announces insurance plan for AI application risks
items.summary: A new Chinese insurance plan reportedly covers third-party losses caused by AI services as well as provider costs linked to model-performance deviations, including repairs and refunds.
